chapter: Learning drums and recording on the Coast
title: Closing tape one and a joke about competing drummers
summary: Smith ends the first session, jokes about both being unemployed drummers, and signs off.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Well, Baby, we'll come back to that inauguration. I know it was one of the high points of your very colorful career, which is still in full bloom, and you and I are still competing for gigs.
Two drummers. Too bad one of us didn't play another instrument, because we would have been together for the last 12 years, and we both know that.
But unfortunately we both play drums.

Well, Baby, I'm going to close this session of the interviewing, and we'll get together soon again and carry on from where we left off with -- I have an outline and questions to ask about people and society as a whole. But I think we've covered your life pretty good up until today.
And as I say, I hope we both get a gig pretty soon, and I'm sure we will. Neither one of us is unemployed very long.
Well, we'll get a gig or either go to the packing house.

Well, Baby, we'll get together soon to carry on these interviews. And now for Baby Lovett, Charles Crook Goodwin, yours truly Art Smith, we're finishing today's interviewing at the After Hours, this is the end of side 2 of tape number 1 for the National Endowment for the Arts of the Smithsonian Institute on Kansas City jazz. Thank you.
